2. The respondents instituted the original suit as plaintiffs for declaration of title to the suit land in the schedule of the plant and subsequently by amendment of the plaint also prayed for recovery of khas possession on alleging that the land measuring 19½ decimals appertaining to mouza-Bagura Alekanda in J.L. No.50 under C.S. Khatian Nos.160 and 178, Plot No.1548 belonged to Gobinda Shil: He executed a will and appointed his wife-Sona Lakhsmi as executrix. Defendant No.3, Ramesh Chandra Shil, was the next reversioner. After the death of Gobinda Chandra Shil, Sona Lakhsmi filed Probate Case No.6 of 1917 before the District Judge, Barisal. Sona Lakhsmi and the reversionar heir leased out the said land to Dinabandhu Gangopadhya (father of defendant Nos.1 and 2) by patta dated 05.11.1941 for legal necessity and delivered possession thereof. In the said patta by mistake Plot No.1549 was written instead of Plot No.1548, but the boundary and the area of the land were correctly written. Since the said pattan, defendant Nos.1 and 2 had been residing on the suit land by constructing dwelling structures thereon on payment of rent, municipal tax etc. The said defendants transferred the suit property to the plaintiffs by registered sale deed dated 12.05.1970, but in that sale deed also mistakenly Plot No.1549 was written in lieu of Plot No.1548. During R.S. operation, the suit land was wrongly recorded in the name of defendant No.3 and her mother-Sona Lakhsmi although they had never claimed the same. Husband of defendant No.6 in collusion with Sudhir Chandra Dutta, an employee of defendant No.5, constructed structures on Plot No.804, and as such, the plaint was amended incorporating prayer for recovery of khas possession in respect of 'lcha' scheduled land. The collusively pre-pared wrong record in the name of defendant No.3 and her mother has clouded the title of the plaintiffs in the suit land and hence the suit. 

 9. It is admitted by the parties that the suit land measuring 19½ acres appertaining to Plot No.1548 under CS Khatian Nos.160 and 178 situated in Mouza-Bagura Alekanda belonged to one Gobinda Chandra Shil who executed a will on appointing his wife-Sona Lakhsmi as executrix. It is not denied that defendant No.3, Ramesh Chandra Shil was the next reversioner. It is also admitted that after the death of Gobinda Chandra Shil, executrix Sona Lakhsmi obtained an order of probate in Probate Case No.6 of 1917 filed before the District Judge, Barisal. 

 11. On the other hand, the contesting defendant No.6(who is appellant here) denied the aforesaid allegation of the plaintiff and counter claimed that Sona Lakhsmi and others never executed any patta as alleged nor the same was acted upon and not only the plaintiffs but also their predecessor never possessed the said land as alleged and accordingly, the RS Khatian has been prepared in the name of Sona Lakhsmi, whose temporary lessee Bipin Behari, Abdul Aziz and Hiron Kumar Karmaker have been possessing the land in Plot No.1548. It has been further alleged that defendant No.5 took settlement of the suit land from Ramesh Chandra Shil on 29.12.1945 and took the same in his khas possession and thereafter transferred 0.431 acres land in favour of defendant  No.6 by kabala dated 01.09.1969 who mutated her name in suit khatian and has been possessing the same on constructing structures thereon. 

 16. The evidentiary value of those private document can only be evaluated on the basis of adduced evidence by the plaintiffs (respondents). But in the instant case, the plaintiff-respondent neither produced the writer of those private dakhila nor produced any person in whose presence that was written with a view to prove the same. Thus, we have no other alternative but to hold that the plaintiff failed to prove the private dakhila or its content on adducing proper and competent witness. After preparation of SA record of right more than 50/60 years have been elapsed, the plaintiffs (respondents) failed to correct or mutate their names in the suit khatian on the strength of such patta and alleged private rent receipts. From the order sheet dated 09.12.1970 in Bakarganj district mutation case bearing No.179kt of 1957-58, it appears that plaintiff-Abdul Quddus filed the mutation case before the concerned Revenue Circle Officer, Kotwali, Barishal who rejected the mutation objection case on holding that the objector, Abdul Quddus has got no locus standi to file the mutation objection. It is fact that if the plaintiffs (respondents) had really been the custodian of those private dakhilas in that case, they might have submitted the same before the Revenue Circle Officer, but they failed to produce those dakhilas before such officer. Failure to submit those private dakhilas before the Revenue Circle Officer, raised an apprehension as to whether the plaintiffs or their predecessor was at all the custodian of those private documents. 

 17. On the other hand, Ext. Jha(1) shows that the defendants and their predecessor duly mutated their names in suit khatian and have been paying rent to the government through dakhilas (Ext ‘cha’-series). SA and RS records of right have been prepared in the names of the defendant-appellants and their predecessors. Those records of right, mutation, rent receipts, tax receipt in respect of suit land are the evidence of possession, yet title follows possession. Particularly, RS record has been prepared after holding local survey and on ascertaining the existing possession. Thus, the fact of possession and dispossession as has been alleged by the plaintiffs (respondents) is not at all believable which appears to be negated the plaintiffs' prayer for khas possession.
